title: You can actually sleep inside a UFO at this extraordinary UK campsite
excerpt: You can now spend the night in a UFO without leaving the planet.
content:
You can now spend the night in a UFO without leaving the planet.

Apple Camping, near Tenby in Pembrokeshire, offers unusual stays including a flying saucer, converted aircraft and themed geodesic domes.

The UFO remains one of the site’s most eye-catching stays.

The futuristic pod sleeps up to four, with a double bed and two single beds that double as sofas.

Inside are a dining area, wardrobe, kettle and tea and coffee-making facilities.

An outdoor kitchen comes with a microwave, toaster and fridge.

Guests share the cooking, toilet and shower facilities on site.

The UFO is built to immerse guests in its extraterrestrial theme.

It has circular windows, retro games and an escape hatch.

The Western Telegraph previously reported remote-controlled retracting stairs and doors, a smoke machine and a laser display of the night sky.

The UFO has attracted attention for years.

Toby Rhys-Jones, who owned the site at the time, said in 2018 that the UFO took three years and around £100,000 to build.

He called it a "real labour of love" and hoped Apple Camping would become the UK's most unique campsite.

The UFO is one of several unusual stays at the site.

Other stays include the JetStar private jet, an Airbus, Pac-Man-inspired geodomes, the Witch's Hat and the Crate Escape.

The site is less than 10 minutes from beaches and other local attractions.

Apple Camping, a glamping site near Tenby in Pembrokeshire, offers a range of unusual stays, including a flying saucer, converted aircraft, and themed geodesic domes. (Image: Hayston Developments & Planning Ltd.)

Apple Camping also has a colourful history.

When Apple Camping was listed for sale in 2022 for around £1.25 million, the Western Telegraph reported that it included a private jet, flying saucer, converted yacht, submarine, train carriage and geodesic domes.

In 2023, Pembrokeshire County Council considered a retrospective planning application for several site units and facilities, including its "disco chapel".

Councillors approved the application, regularising the glamping attraction’s developments.

The applicant’s agent told councillors the site had become a "quirky tourism" success after appearing on television and in the national press.

In 2026, Apple Camping continues to welcome families, groups and guests with dogs.

The site describes itself as a family-run retreat near the Pembrokeshire coast.

Apple Camping says it aims to give visitors an unusual base for exploring Pembrokeshire.

When the site was put on the market in 2022, the sale included 15 glamping accommodations, a five-bedroom farmhouse, a facilities building, workshop, disco church and ample parking.
